title: Working with the Event Monitoring & Notification API

blocks.text: This article explains how you can discover available event sources and create subscriptions to receive notifications when specific events occur in your Zscaler environment. The Event Monitoring & Notification API supports automated delivery of notifications using multiple channels, including email, webhook, and Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS).
Organizations must meet the following prerequisites before they can create and manage subscriptions:

blocks.item: Ensure that you have the Event Monitoring & Notification API service enabled for your tenant. To obtain access to this API service, contact your Zscaler Account team.

Register the API client application in Authentication Service and assign the Event Monitoring Subscribe role. This role provides view-only access to the service catalog and full access to subscriptions (i.e., create, update, and delete) within the Event Monitoring & Notification API.

Assign a role from the API product resource for which the notifications are subscribed. Currently, you can subscribe to notifications for ZPA, so a role from the ZPA product resource must be assigned.

blocks.text: To learn more about the API client setup and different authentication methods, see Getting Started. To learn how to register a client in Authentication Service, see Adding an API Client and Viewing API Resources.

After your API client is created and provisioned in Authentication Service, the next step is to authenticate using the client's generated credentials. Authentication verifies your client's identity and issues an access token that must be sent in every subsequent API request using the Authorization header (i.e., Authorization: Bearer <Token>). To learn more, see Getting Started.

blocks.text: In this step, you can select which events you want to subscribe to and configure notification channels using an API request. You can subscribe to multiple source types and events within a single subscription.
The request specifies the event details within the scope object:

blocks.item: source_key: The source to be monitored for events (e.g., zpa)
source_type_key: The specific source type within that source (e.g., app_connector)
source_event_key: The specific events for which you want to receive alerts (e.g., status)

blocks.text: In addition, all subscription API calls require the following headers to identify the product tenant that you want to monitor:

blocks.item: x-em-cloud: Cloud identifier for the product tenant (e.g., prod.zpath.net)
x-em-tenant: Product tenant identifier for ZIA, ZPA, etc. (e.g., 145254691217866752)

The following steps outline an end-to-end setup and workflow for creating subscriptions using Amazon SNS:

blocks.item: Verify that SNS is available as a channel: Send a GET request to /subscriptions/channels and confirm that the sns channel is supported for your tenant.

Retrieve SNS setup requirements: Send a GET request to /subscriptions/channels/sns to obtain the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for the Zscaler Identity and Access Management (IAM) role, required permissions, and the SNS topic policy template.
Create an SNS topic in your AWS account: Create a topic using the Amazon Web Services (AWS) SNS console, AWS CLI, or AWS CloudFormation (Standard or First-In-First-Out (FIFO), as required).
Apply the SNS topic policy: Associate a topic policy that grants the Zscaler IAM role permission to publish to your topic (for example, using aws sns set-topic-attributes).
Verify that Zscaler can access the topic: Send a POST request to /subscriptions/channels/sns:verify to confirm that the Event Monitoring & Notification API can access and publish to your SNS topic.
Create the Event Monitoring subscription: Send a POST request to /subscriptions to create a subscription that uses the sns channel.

blocks.text: After completing these steps, you will start receiving events on your SNS topic. When alert conditions are met, the Event Monitoring & Notification API publishes events to your topic asynchronously. Your SNS subscriptions then deliver messages to downstream systems (e.g., Amazon SQS, Amazon Lambda, and HTTP/HTTPS endpoints) according to your configuration.
Use GET /subscriptions/channels to retrieve the list of all notification channel types supported for your tenant, shown as follows.
Example request:

blocks.code:
GET /subscriptions/channels HTTP/1.1
Host: api.zsapi.net
Authorization: Bearer <access-token>

blocks.text: Example response (200 OK):

The sns entry with "setup_required": true indicates that additional configuration is needed before you can use the SNS channel. Follow the self link (/subscriptions/channels/sns) to view the SNS-specific setup requirements.
Use GET /subscriptions/channels/sns to retrieve the Zscaler IAM role ARN, the minimum required permissions, and a ready‑to‑use SNS topic policy template that you can apply to your SNS topic.
Example request:

blocks.code:
GET /subscriptions/channels/sns HTTP/1.1
Host: api.zsapi.net
Authorization: Bearer <access-token>

blocks.text: Example response (200 OK)
From the response:

blocks.item: Note the zscaler_role_arn value. This is the Zscaler IAM role that will publish to your SNS topic.
Use sns_topic_policy_template when configuring your SNS topic policy in the next step.
Replace <customer_topic_arn> with the ARN of your SNS topic.

blocks.text: Create an SNS topic in your AWS account for receiving notifications. Both Standard topics and FIFO topics (with a .fifo suffix) are supported.
To learn how to create SNS topics, refer to the Amazon documentation.
AWS CLI examples

blocks.code:
# Standard topic
aws sns create-topic \
  --name zscaler-em-events \
  --region us-west-2

# FIFO topic (name must end with `.fifo`)
aws sns create-topic \
  --name zscaler-em-events.fifo \
  --attributes FifoTopic=true,ContentBasedDeduplication=true \
  --region us-west-2

blocks.heading: Step 5: Verify that Zscaler Can Publish

blocks.text: Use POST /subscriptions/channels/sns:verify to validate that Zscaler can successfully call sns:GetTopicAttributes on your SNS topic. This is a read-only check; no test message is published to the topic.
Example request:

blocks.code:
POST /subscriptions/channels/sns:verify HTTP/1.1
Host: api.zsapi.net
Authorization: Bearer <access-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "topic_arn": "arn:aws:sns:us-west-2:123456789012:zscaler-em-events",
  "region": "us-west-2"
}

Internal error in the Event Monitoring & Notification API service (not caused by the request).
Indicates a Zscaler-side issue. Wait briefly and retry with backoff. If the error continues, contact Zscaler Support.

blocks.text: After SNS verification succeeds, use POST /subscriptions to create an event subscription that forwards specific events (e.g., ZPA App Connector status changes) to your SNS topic.
Example request:
You can attach multiple channels (for example, email, webhook, and SNS) to a single subscription. Each qualifying event is delivered to all configured channels.

When the Event Monitoring & Notification API delivers an event to your SNS topic, Amazon SNS wraps the Zscaler event in a standard SNS envelope. The Zscaler event JSON is delivered as a string in the Message field.

The following example request shows how to update an existing subscription.

blocks.code:
curl -X PUT https://api.zsapi.net/event-monitoring/subscriptions/<subscription-id> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <Token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-em-cloud: prod.zpath.net" \
  -H "x-em-tenant: 145254691217866752" \
  -d '{ ... updated subscription body ... }

blocks.text: Set "enabled": false in the update request to temporarily disable a subscription without deleting it. When a subscription is disabled, notifications are no longer sent, but the subscription configuration is preserved.

blocks.item: TLS required: All data in transit must be encrypted.
Tenant isolation: Isolation is enforced by authorization constraints and tenant mapping validation.
Audit logging: All operations log tenant ID, trace ID, API client ID, client IP address, and the change details (i.e., what was created, updated, or deleted).

blocks.text: The following sections provide troubleshooting tips for common issues encountered when operating, integrating with, or developing using the Event Monitoring & Notification API service to create and manage subscriptions.
Try the following:

blocks.item: Check your subscription enablement status by sending a GET /subscriptions/{id} request with your subscription ID and verifying the "enabled": true setting in the response.
Check the scope to ensure that source_key, source_type_key, and source_event_key match the events being produced.
Check your subscription's product tenant ID (i.e., zpa_tenant_id) to verify what the subscription is for.

blocks.text: Verify that the email address matches the expected format: ^[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$
Try the following:

blocks.item: Verify that the URL matches the expected format: ^https?://.+$
Ensure that the webhook endpoint is reachable from the API deployment network.
Check for TLS certificate issues when using HTTPS.
